messages.content:
Hi everyone,

I've been thinking about the goals set for this competition, and I'm curious about two things:

  1. Is anyone explicitly targeting a perfect 100% score, rather than just improving incrementally over the current best of your team? If your approach is built around maximizing correctness across the full test set rather than squeezing out a few extra points on public leaderboard, I'd love to hear about your strategy.

  2. Has anyone done (or considered doing) a formal feasibility study for this competition — analyzing things like:

    • the theoretical upper bound of current approaches(specifically about LLMs) on this task distribution
    • whether the full test set is learnable/solvable within the compute(g4-standard-48) and time constraints(9 hours)
    • what the bottleneck actually is: reasoning, data, compute, or evaluation design

I'm not assuming 100% is achievable — I genuinely don't know. But before everyone converges on "just beat the leaderboard baseline," it might be valuable to understand where the ceiling really is.

If you're working on either of these, or have thoughts on why this framing is flawed, please share!
